Q: Passing nlohmann::json objects by value A:

The parse() function has to return by value. What you get back is the only instance of the internal representation of the JSON data you've parsed that exists.

It's when you then pass the value (or a sub-value) you get from parse() on to other functions that you should be careful to not copy unless you actually want a separate copy to work on. You'd usually pass a const or non-const reference to the json value instead.

Q: Best way to go from JSON to bash variables A:

Mapping json to bash array, using jq

Using bashisms and playing with array could be nice:

#!/bin/bash

wantedVars=( foo bar foobar )

json=$'{
        "data": {
            "foo": "bar baz",
            "bar": "Don\47t miss miximg quotes and double quotes: \47\\"\47!",
            "baz": "ping",
            "foobar": 42
        }
}'

declare -A "fromJson=($(jq --raw-output <<<"$json" '
        .data |
        to_entries |
        map( "[\( .key | @sh )]=\( .value | @sh )" ) |
        .[]
' ))"

for var in "${wantedVars[@]}";do
   printf -v "$var" '%s' "${fromJson["$var"]}"
done

printf '%-10s|%s|\n' foo: "$foo" bar: "$bar" foobar: "$foobar"

Should produce:

foo:      |bar baz|
bar:      |Don't miss miximg quotes and double quotes: '"'!|
foobar:   |42|

( Note that hardcoded last line could be replaced by:

for var in "${wantedVars[@]}";do
    printf '%-10s|%s|\n' "$var" "${!var}"
done

will render same output ;-)

Into a function:

Then we could imagine this as a function:

#!/bin/bash

wantedVars=( foo bar foobar )

json=$'{
        "data": {
            "foo": "bar baz",
            "bar": "Don\47t miss miximg quotes and double quotes: \47\\"\47!",
            "baz": "ping",
            "foobar": 42
        }
}'

json2Vars() {
    local var
    local -A "fromJson=($(jq --raw-output '
        .data |
        to_entries |
        map( "[\( .key | @sh )]=\( .value | @sh )" ) |
        .[]
    ' ))"
    for var; do
        printf -v "$var" '%s' "${fromJson["$var"]}"
    done
}

json2Vars "${wantedVars[@]}" <<<"$json" 

for var in "${wantedVars[@]}"; do
    printf '%-10s|%s|\n' "$var:" "${!var}"
done

Q: Dashboard Setup: Same Repo or Separate Project? A:

There's no need to create a new repository; if you want to reuse a dashboard in different areas of your project, simply use namespaces.

PATH: Controllers/Admin/DashboardController.php

namespace App\Http\Controllers\Admin;

PATH: Controllers/DashboardController.php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

Q: Use local program on docker A:

I'm not sure how to ask this question

If you get prompted for a question type, always pick "troubleshooting". The other question choices activate an experimental UI that has some serious bugs (for example, I cannot write this as a comment) and is not getting any bug fixes. You'd need to delete and recreate this question to use the standard question UI ("you can't change the question type" is another months-old bug). Make sure to see the help center for advice on writing a good-quality question.

Is there a way to make docker use them without having to install them in Docker? Like updating a PATH variable or something similar?

No. By design a container can't see files on the host system. A best practice would be to install them in your image's Dockerfile, so that you don't have to have them installed on the host system.

Other answers have suggested a bind mount, but this won't work well if the host programs have library dependencies or need files in system directories like /etc or /var. This also means your container has a dependency on specific things existing on the host, which a container setup will usually avoid.

The standard way for one container to invoke another is via a network connection, so if one container is running an HTTP or gRPC server then another could call it. It looks like OpenFOAM is mostly a collection of command-line tools, and it's hard and often insecure for one container to try to run a command-line tool in another. If FreeCAD is a GUI program, it won't run well in a container at all.

Q: Rendering many connected quarto documents A:

You can modify an involved knitr-hook to save the state of the R environment at the end of a document render.

The code: https://gist.github.com/willgryan/6c8bb8fe1a394917d4779d2ca7ef09e7
Only one small code file, and a few lines at the start of every .qmd file which should share an environment. Elegant and compact.

The reason for this difference between Quarto and R markdown is how a document is composed. R markdown supported the merge-knit multi-file approach, currently not supported natively by Quarto.

Q: Toggle case of next letter in elisp A:

I couldn't get @abo-abo's answer working for me but using his comments I was able to google better and found the following at https://leahneukirchen.org/dotfiles/.emacs

(defun leah2-toggle-case ()
  (interactive)
  (let ((char (following-char)))
    (if (eq char (upcase char))
        (insert-char (downcase char) 1 t)
      (insert-char (upcase char) 1 t)))
  (delete-char 1 nil)
  (backward-char))
(leah2-define-key "M-#" 'leah2-toggle-case)

This answers the original question if you remove (backward-char).
